title: Suspected broken bone in an arm or leg
summary: Severe pain, swelling, deformity, or inability to use a limb after an injury suggests a possible fracture. Stop using it, immobilise it, and get to medical care.
steps: Keep the person still and reassure them.
Do not try to straighten or push back a bone — support the limb in the position you found it.
Steady the limb above and below the suspected break with your hands, or with rolled cloths, towels, or a folded magazine taped beside the limb as a splint.
For an arm injury, support the arm against the body with a sling made from a triangular cloth, or rest it on a cushion in the lap.
For a leg injury, do not let the person walk on it. Pad between the legs and gently bind the injured leg to the uninjured one if transport is long.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in a cloth for 15–20 minutes to reduce swelling.
Arrange transport to a clinic or emergency department. Keep the person warm and do not give food or drink in case anaesthesia is needed.
avoid: Do not try to push a bone back under the skin if it is sticking out — cover it with a clean cloth and go to emergency.
Do not give the person food or drink.
Do not move them unnecessarily, especially if the back, neck, or hip might be injured.
Do not apply heat to a fresh injury for the first 24–48 hours.
whenToEscalate: Always — suspected fractures need an X-ray and proper alignment.
Emergency immediately if: bone is showing through the skin, the limb looks deformed, the hand or foot below the injury is cold, blue, or numb, or there is heavy bleeding.
Suspected hip, pelvis, spine, or skull fracture — do not move the person unless absolutely necessary; call emergency.
